entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Chen Lin (c. 160 CE – 217 CE), a preeminent literatus and official, played a crucial role in the political and literary landscape of the late Eastern Han dynasty and the tumultuous Three Kingdoms period in China. Born in Guangling Commandery (modern-day Baoying County, Jiangsu), Chen Lin distinguished himself through his exceptional skill in crafting polemical prose and rhapsodies (fu). His career spanned service under the powerful warlord Yuan Shao and later, the formidable Cao Cao, placing him at the heart of the era's grand political struggles and cultural flourishing. He is recognized as one of the "Seven Masters of Jian'an" (建安七子), a group of influential poets and writers whose work defined the literary style of their age.

Chen Lin's most famous work, the 'Proclamation Against Cao Cao for Yuan Shao' (為袁紹檄豫州文), stands as a masterpiece of invective literature. Composed around 200 CE, this highly detailed and scathing denunciation of Cao Cao's character and ancestry was so potent that, legend claims, it cured Cao Cao of a headache upon reading it. After Yuan Shao's defeat at the Battle of Guandu, Chen Lin was captured but spared by Cao Cao, who admired his literary talent. He subsequently joined Cao Cao's secretariat, continuing to produce important official documents, memorials, and literary pieces, including a historical work on the Han dynasty, further solidifying his reputation as a master of prose and rhetoric.
